items.stem: Explain why logₐ(xy) = logₐ x + logₐ y, using the laws of indices.
items.answer: Let x = aᵖ and y = a^q. Then xy = a^(p + q), so logₐ(xy) = p + q = logₐ x + logₐ y.

items.stem: Aisha writes log 16 − log 4 = (log 16)/(log 4). Explain the error and simplify log 16 − log 4 correctly.

items.stem: Explain why logₐ a = 1 and logₐ(1/a) = −1.

items.stem: Tomás writes log₃ 3 + log₃ 9 = log₃ 12. Explain the error and find the correct value of log₃ 3 + log₃ 9.

items.stem: Explain why plotting ln y against ln x is useful for testing whether data fit a model y = kxⁿ.

items.stem: Explain how to tell, from the graph of ln y against x, whether y = Abˣ describes growth or decay.

items.stem: Ines writes log 10 − log 2 = (log 10)/(log 2). Explain the error and simplify log 10 − log 2 correctly.
items.answer: Subtracting logarithms gives the log of the quotient: log 10 − log 2 = log(10/2) = log 5. It is not a quotient of logarithms.
items.markingKey: B1 log a − log b = log(a/b); B1 log 5 [2]

items.stem: Simplify e^(3 ln 2).
Tomás solves e³ˣ = 20 and writes x = ln(20/3). Explain the error and give the correct solution in exact form.
items.answer: Taking ln of both sides gives 3x = ln 20, so x = (ln 20)/3 = 0.999; ln(20/3) = ln 20 − ln 3 is different.

items.stem: Grace solves e^(2x) + 5eˣ + 6 = 0 by factorising to (eˣ + 2)(eˣ + 3) = 0 and writes x = ln(−2) or x = ln(−3). Explain why the equation has no real solutions.
items.answer: eˣ > 0 for all real x, so eˣ = −2 and eˣ = −3 are impossible; ln of a negative number is undefined. Hence there are no real solutions.
items.markingKey: B1 eˣ > 0 always; B1 so neither factor can be zero: no real solutions [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) When solving 0.6ⁿ < 0.01 by taking logarithms, what happens to the inequality sign when dividing by ln 0.6? (b) Which expression gives the solution of 3ˣ = 7?
items.answer: (a) It reverses, because ln 0.6 < 0 (b) x = ln 7 / ln 3
items.markingKey: (a) Dividing by a negative number reverses an inequality. (b) Take logs: x ln 3 = ln 7.

items.stem: Elena solves 5 × 3ˣ = 190 by writing 15ˣ = 190. Explain the error and solve the equation correctly, giving x to 3 significant figures.
items.answer: 5 × 3ˣ is not (5 × 3)ˣ; divide first: 3ˣ = 38, x = ln 38 / ln 3 = 3.31.
items.markingKey: B1 must divide by 5 first (only 3 is raised to the power x); M1 x = ln 38/ln 3; A1 3.31 [3]

items.stem: For the model y = kxⁿ, the graph of ln y against ln x is a straight line through (1.15, −0.45) and (2.51, −3.85). Nadia finds the intercept 2.42 and states that k = 2.42. Explain the error and find k.
items.answer: The intercept is ln k, not k. ln k = 2.42, so k = e^2.42 = 11.3.
items.markingKey: B1 intercept = ln k; B1 k = 11.3 [2]
